name: Mate
description: Mate is a traditional Italian fishing card game played with a 40-card Italian deck. Players capture cards from a central layout by matching values, with special scoring for capturing the 'Mate' cards (Kings). It is a game of memory and timing, where players must remember which cards have been played to maximize their captures.

history.origins: Originating in Italy, Mate belongs to the family of fishing games popular throughout the Mediterranean. It shares mechanics with Scopa and other Italian card games.
timeline: Traditional: Played for generations in Italian households
19th Century: Documented in Italian game collections
Present: Still played in Italy and by Italian communities worldwide

setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck (remove 8s, 9s, 10s from standard deck). Suits: Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs. Ranking: King (highest), Queen, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, Ace (lowest).
setup.dealing: 4 cards to each player and 4 cards face-up to the table. Remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: 40-card Italian deck or modified standard deck.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table by matching their values. Score points for capturing specific cards (Kings, the 7 of Coins, etc.) and for capturing the most cards overall.
rules.gameplay: 1. Players take turns playing one card from hand to the table. 2. If the played card matches the value of a card on the table, the player captures both cards. 3. Multiple cards can be captured if their values sum to the played card's value. 4. If no capture is possible, the card remains on the table. 5. After playing, players draw a replacement card from the stock if available.
keyRules: Score for specific captured cards and sweeps

strategy.basic: Remember which cards have been played. Try to capture Kings and the 7 of Coins. Avoid leaving valuable cards on the table for opponents to capture.
strategy.intermediate: Set up sweeps by leaving specific card combinations on the table that you can capture on your next turn. Force opponents to play cards that benefit you.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential. Track all high-value cards to predict opponents' holdings. Sacrifice immediate captures to set up multiple captures or sweeps.
tips: The 7 of Coins is usually the most valuable single card - prioritize capturing it
Leaving a single low card on the table is safer than multiple cards that can be combined
When you have multiple capture options, choose the one that leaves the table least favorable for opponents

scoring.description: Points are awarded for: each King captured (1 point), the 7 of Coins (1 point), capturing the majority of cards (1 point), and each sweep/scopa (1 point).
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach a target score (typically 11 or 21 points) wins, or highest score when stock is exhausted.
